entries.name: map()
entries.description: Creates a new array populated with the results of calling a provided function on every element in the calling array. Does not mutate the original array.
entries.syntax:
array.map(callbackFn)
array.map(callbackFn, thisArg)

callbackFn(element, index, array)

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: A function called for each element. Receives (element, index, array).

parameters.name: thisArg
parameters.description: Value to use as 'this' when executing callbackFn.

examples.title: Double each number
Transform objects
Use index

commonMistakes: Forgetting that map() always returns an array of the same length
Using map() when you need side effects — use forEach() instead
Mutating the original array inside the callback
bestPractices: Use map() only when you need the returned array
Prefer arrow functions for concise transformations
entries.performanceNotes: O(n) — iterates every element once. For very large arrays, consider typed arrays or generator-based approaches.

entries.name: filter()
entries.description: Creates a new array with all elements that pass the test implemented by the provided function. Does not mutate the original array.
entries.syntax:
array.filter(callbackFn)
array.filter(callbackFn, thisArg)

callbackFn(element, index, array) → boolean

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: A predicate function. Elements that return true are kept.

parameters.name: thisArg
parameters.description: Value to use as 'this' when executing callbackFn.

examples.title: Filter even numbers
Filter objects by property
Remove falsy values

commonMistakes: Returning a value other than boolean (truthy/falsy still works)
Expecting filter to mutate the original array
bestPractices: Combine with map() for filter-then-transform pipelines
Use Boolean as callback to remove all falsy values

entries.name: reduce()
entries.description: Executes a user-supplied reducer callback function on each element of the array, passing in the return value from the previous call. Returns a single accumulated value.
entries.syntax:
array.reduce(callbackFn)
array.reduce(callbackFn, initialValue)

callbackFn(accumulator, currentValue, index, array) → newAccumulator

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Reducer function called for each element. Receives (accumulator, currentValue, index, array).

parameters.name: initialValue
parameters.description: The initial value of the accumulator. If omitted, the first element is used.

examples.title: Sum an array
Group by property
Flatten one level

commonMistakes: Forgetting the initialValue when reducing to an object or array
Not returning the accumulator from the callback
Using reduce when map/filter is clearer
bestPractices: Always provide initialValue to avoid bugs on empty arrays
Use Object.groupBy() (ES2024) for grouping when available

entries.name: forEach()
entries.description: Executes a provided function once for each array element. Unlike map(), it does not return a value. Use it for side effects.
entries.syntax:
array.forEach(callbackFn)
array.forEach(callbackFn, thisArg)

callbackFn(element, index, array)

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Function called for each element.

parameters.name: thisArg
parameters.description: Value to use as 'this'.

examples.title: Log each item
Update DOM elements
examples.code:
const items = document.querySelectorAll('.item');
items.forEach(item => item.classList.add('highlighted'));

commonMistakes: Using forEach when map() is needed (expecting a return value)
Trying to break out of forEach — use for...of instead
bestPractices: Use for...of when you need break/continue
Use map() when you need the transformed array

entries.name: find()
entries.description: Returns the first element in the array that satisfies the provided testing function. Returns undefined if no element satisfies the test.
entries.syntax:
array.find(callbackFn)
array.find(callbackFn, thisArg)

callbackFn(element, index, array) → boolean

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Predicate function. Called for each element until it returns true.

examples.title: Find by property
Find first even number

useCases: Locating the first match in a list
commonMistakes: Not handling the undefined case when no match is found
bestPractices: Use optional chaining (?.) on the result to avoid errors when undefined

entries.name: findIndex()
entries.description: Returns the index of the first element that satisfies the testing function. Returns -1 if no element passes.

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Predicate that returns true for the target element.

examples.title: Find index by value

useCases: Finding position to splice/replace an element
commonMistakes: Confusing -1 return with a valid index

entries.name: findLast()
entries.description: Returns the last element that satisfies the provided testing function, iterating from right to left. Returns undefined if not found.

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Predicate that returns true for the target element.

examples.title: Find last even

entries.name: some()
entries.description: Tests whether at least one element in the array passes the test. Returns true on first match; does not iterate further.

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Predicate function.

examples.title: Check if any negative

entries.complexity: O(n) worst case, short-circuits on first match

entries.name: every()
entries.description: Tests whether all elements in the array pass the test. Returns false and short-circuits on the first failure.

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Predicate function.

examples.title: All positive check

useCases: Checking all items meet a condition

entries.name: sort()
entries.description: Sorts the elements of an array in place. The default sort is by UTF-16 code units — always provide a comparator for numbers and complex objects.
entries.syntax:
array.sort()
array.sort(compareFn)

compareFn(a, b) → number
  negative → a before b
  zero → order unchanged
  positive → b before a

parameters.name: compareFn
parameters.description: Comparison function. Should return a negative, zero, or positive number.

examples.title: Sort numbers ascending
Sort strings alphabetically
Sort objects by property

commonMistakes: Using default sort for numbers — [10, 9, 2] sorts as ['10', '2', '9'] without compareFn
Forgetting sort() mutates the original array — use toSorted() to avoid mutation
bestPractices: Always provide a compareFn for non-string sorting
Use toSorted() when immutability is required

entries.name: toSorted()
entries.description: Returns a new sorted array without modifying the original. The immutable version of sort().

parameters.name: compareFn
parameters.description: Comparison function returning negative, zero, or positive.

examples.title: Non-destructive sort

entries.name: slice()
entries.description: Returns a shallow copy of a portion of an array. Does not modify the original.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Zero-based index to start extraction. Negative values count from end.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Index before which to stop. Not included. Negative values count from end.

examples.title: Take first three elements
examples.code:
const arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
console.log(arr.slice(0, 3)); // [1, 2, 3]

examples.title: Take last two elements
examples.code:
const arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
console.log(arr.slice(-2)); // [4, 5]

examples.title: Clone an array

entries.complexity: O(k) where k is the size of the slice

entries.name: splice()
entries.description: Changes the contents of an array by removing, replacing, or inserting elements in place.
entries.syntax:
array.splice(start)
array.splice(start, deleteCount)
array.splice(start, deleteCount, item1, item2, ...)

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Index at which to start changing the array.

parameters.name: deleteCount
parameters.description: Number of elements to remove. If 0, no elements are removed.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Elements to add to the array at start.

examples.title: Remove elements
Insert elements
Replace elements

entries.complexity: O(n) in worst case due to shifting
commonMistakes: Confusing splice() (mutates) with slice() (returns copy)

entries.name: flat()
entries.description: Creates a new array with all sub-array elements concatenated into it recursively up to the specified depth.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Specifies how many levels to flatten. Defaults to 1. Use Infinity to flatten completely.

examples.title: Flatten completely
examples.code:
const deep = [1, [2, [3, [4]]]];
console.log(deep.flat(Infinity)); // [1, 2, 3, 4]

entries.complexity: O(n) where n is total elements

entries.name: flatMap()
entries.description: Maps each element using a function, then flattens the result by one level. More efficient than calling map() followed by flat(1).
entries.syntax:
array.flatMap(callbackFn)
callbackFn(element, index, array) → Array | value

parameters.name: callbackFn
parameters.description: Function that returns an array or value for each element.

examples.title: Split words then flatten
Conditional expansion

entries.name: concat()
entries.description: Returns a new array formed by merging two or more arrays. Does not mutate existing arrays.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Arrays or values to concatenate.

examples.title: Merge two arrays
Spread alternative
examples.code: const merged = [...a, ...b]; // preferred modern approach

entries.name: includes()
entries.description: Determines whether an array includes a certain value among its entries, returning true or false. Uses SameValueZero comparison (NaN-safe).

parameters.name: searchElement
parameters.description: The value to search for.

parameters.name: fromIndex
parameters.description: Starting index for the search. Negative counts from end.

examples.title: Check membership
NaN check

entries.name: at()
entries.description: Returns the element at the given index. Accepts negative integers counting from the end of the array.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Zero-based index. Negative values count from end: -1 is last element.

examples.title: Access last element

entries.name: push()
entries.description: Adds one or more elements to the end of an array and returns the new length.

parameters.name: elements
parameters.description: Elements to add to the end of the array.

examples.title: Add elements

entries.name: pop()
entries.description: Removes the last element from an array and returns it. Mutates the array.

examples.title: Remove last item

entries.name: join()
entries.description: Joins all elements of an array into a string, separated by a specified separator. null and undefined are converted to empty strings.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: String to put between elements. Defaults to comma.

examples.title: Join with separator
Build path
examples.code:
const segments = ['usr', 'local', 'bin'];
console.log(segments.join('/')); // 'usr/local/bin'

entries.name: split()
entries.description: Divides a string into an ordered list of substrings by searching for a separator, and returns an array of these substrings.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: Pattern describing where each split should occur.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of substrings to return.

examples.title: Split by character
examples.code:
const str = 'a,b,c,d';
console.log(str.split(',')); // ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']

examples.title: Split into characters
examples.code:
const str = 'hello';
console.log(str.split('')); // ['h', 'e', 'l', 'l', 'o']

examples.title: Split words
examples.code:
const sentence = 'Hello World Foo';
console.log(sentence.split(' ')); // ['Hello', 'World', 'Foo']

entries.name: trim()
entries.description: Removes whitespace from both ends of a string. Returns a new string without modifying the original.

examples.title: Trim whitespace
examples.code:
const str = '  hello world  ';
console.log(str.trim()); // 'hello world'

entries.name: replace()
entries.description: Returns a new string with the first occurrence (or all occurrences with a global regex) of a pattern replaced by a replacement string or function.
entries.syntax:
str.replace(pattern, replacement)

pattern: string | RegExp
replacement: string | Function

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The substring or regex to find.

parameters.name: replacement
parameters.description: Replacement string or function returning a string.

examples.title: Replace first occurrence
examples.code:
const str = 'Hello World World';
console.log(str.replace('World', 'JS')); // 'Hello JS World'

examples.title: Replace all with regex
examples.code:
const str = 'foo bar foo';
console.log(str.replace(/foo/g, 'baz')); // 'baz bar baz'

examples.title: Use function replacement

entries.name: replaceAll()
entries.description: Returns a new string with all occurrences of a pattern replaced. Simpler than using a global regex with replace().

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: String or RegExp (must have global flag if regex).

parameters.name: replacement
parameters.description: Replacement string or function.

examples.title: Replace all occurrences
examples.code:
const str = 'cat and cat and cat';
console.log(str.replaceAll('cat', 'dog')); // 'dog and dog and dog'

entries.name: includes()
entries.description: Determines whether one string may be found within another string. Case-sensitive.

parameters.name: searchString
parameters.description: The substring to search for.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Position in the string at which to begin searching. Defaults to 0.

examples.title: Check for substring

entries.name: startsWith()
entries.description: Determines whether a string begins with the characters of a specified string. Case-sensitive.

parameters.name: searchString
parameters.description: The characters to search for at the start.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Position to start the search from. Defaults to 0.

examples.title: Check prefix

entries.complexity: O(k) where k is searchString length

entries.name: endsWith()
entries.description: Determines whether a string ends with the characters of a specified string.

parameters.name: searchString
parameters.description: The characters to search for at the end.

parameters.name: endPosition
parameters.description: The length of the string to search. Defaults to str.length.

examples.title: Check file extension

entries.name: padStart()
entries.description: Pads the current string with another string (repeated if needed) to reach a given length, from the start of the string.

parameters.name: targetLength
parameters.description: The length of the resulting string.

parameters.name: padString
parameters.description: String to pad with. Defaults to space.

examples.title: Zero-pad numbers
examples.code:
const num = '5';
console.log(num.padStart(3, '0')); // '005'

examples.title: Format time

entries.name: slice()
entries.description: Extracts a section of a string and returns it as a new string. Negative indices count from the end.

parameters.name: beginIndex
parameters.description: Zero-based index to begin extraction. Negative counts from end.

parameters.name: endIndex
parameters.description: Index before which to end. Not included. Negative counts from end.

examples.title: Extract substring

entries.name: Object.keys()
entries.description: Returns an array of a given object's own enumerable string-keyed property names.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The object whose enumerable own properties are to be returned.

examples.title: Get property names
examples.code:
const user = { name: 'Alice', age: 30, active: true };
console.log(Object.keys(user)); // ['name', 'age', 'active']

examples.title: Iterate over properties

entries.name: Object.values()
entries.description: Returns an array of a given object's own enumerable string-keyed property values.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The object whose enumerable own property values are to be returned.

examples.title: Get all values

entries.name: Object.entries()
entries.description: Returns an array of a given object's own enumerable string-keyed [key, value] pairs.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The object whose entries are to be returned.

examples.title: Iterate key-value pairs
Convert to Map

entries.name: Object.assign()
entries.description: Copies all enumerable own properties from one or more source objects to a target object. Returns the modified target.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The target object to copy into. It is modified and returned.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Source objects to copy properties from.

examples.title: Merge objects
Shallow clone

entries.complexity: O(n) where n is total properties
commonMistakes: Shallow copy only — nested objects are still shared by reference
Overwriting the target — use {} as first argument to avoid mutation
bestPractices: Prefer spread syntax {...a, ...b} for a more declarative approach

entries.name: Object.freeze()
entries.description: Freezes an object, making it immutable: new properties cannot be added, existing properties cannot be removed or reconfigured, and their values cannot be changed.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The object to freeze.

examples.title: Immutable config

commonMistakes: freeze() is shallow — nested objects are still mutable
Expecting errors without strict mode — fails silently otherwise

entries.name: Object.fromEntries()
entries.description: Transforms a list of key-value pairs into an object. Inverse of Object.entries().

parameters.name: iterable
parameters.description: An iterable (e.g. Array or Map) of [key, value] pairs.

examples.title: From entries array
Transform object values

entries.name: Promise.all()
entries.description: Takes an iterable of promises and returns a new promise that resolves when all input promises resolve, with an array of all resolved values. Rejects immediately if any input promise rejects.

parameters.name: iterable
parameters.description: An iterable (e.g. Array) of promises.

examples.title: Parallel API calls
Process results

commonMistakes: Using Promise.all when one failure should not cancel others — use Promise.allSettled instead
bestPractices: Use for independent parallel operations where all must succeed
Use Promise.allSettled when partial results are acceptable

entries.name: Promise.allSettled()
entries.description: Returns a promise that resolves after all given promises settle (either fulfill or reject). Returns an array of objects describing the outcome of each promise.

parameters.name: iterable
parameters.description: Iterable of promises.

examples.title: Handle partial failures

entries.name: Promise.race()
entries.description: Returns a promise that settles with the outcome of the first input promise to settle (whether fulfilled or rejected).

parameters.name: iterable
parameters.description: Iterable of promises.

examples.title: Timeout pattern

entries.name: Promise.any()
entries.description: Takes an iterable of promises. Returns a promise that fulfills when any of the input promises fulfills. Rejects with an AggregateError only if all promises reject.

parameters.name: iterable
parameters.description: Iterable of promises.

examples.title: First successful fetch

entries.name: JSON.parse()
entries.description: Parses a JSON string and returns the JavaScript value described by the string.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The JSON string to parse.

parameters.name: reviver
parameters.description: Optional function to transform parsed values.

examples.title: Parse JSON string
Safe parse with try/catch

commonMistakes: Not wrapping in try/catch — invalid JSON throws SyntaxError
bestPractices: Always validate/parse with try/catch when input is external

entries.name: JSON.stringify()
entries.description: Converts a JavaScript value to a JSON string. Undefined, function, and symbol values are omitted from the output.
entries.syntax:
JSON.stringify(value)
JSON.stringify(value, replacer)
JSON.stringify(value, replacer, space)

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to serialize.

parameters.name: replacer
parameters.description: Array of allowed keys or transform function.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Spaces for indentation in the output string.

examples.title: Serialize to JSON
examples.code:
const user = { name: 'Alice', age: 30 };
console.log(JSON.stringify(user)); // '{"name":"Alice","age":30}'

examples.title: Pretty print

entries.name: Math.max()
entries.description: Returns the largest of zero or more numbers. Returns -Infinity when called with no arguments.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Numbers to compare.

examples.title: Find maximum
examples.code:
console.log(Math.max(1, 3, 2)); // 3
console.log(Math.max(-5, -2, -8)); // -2

examples.title: Max from array
examples.code:
const numbers = [4, 2, 9, 1, 7];
console.log(Math.max(...numbers)); // 9

entries.name: Math.min()
entries.description: Returns the smallest of zero or more numbers.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Numbers to compare.

examples.title: Find minimum

entries.name: Math.floor()
entries.description: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to a given number (rounds down).

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: A number.

examples.title: Round down
examples.code:
console.log(Math.floor(4.7)); // 4
console.log(Math.floor(-4.7)); // -5
console.log(Math.floor(Math.random() * 10)); // Random 0-9

entries.name: Math.random()
entries.description: Returns a floating-point pseudo-random number in the range [0, 1). Not cryptographically secure — use crypto.getRandomValues() for security.

examples.title: Random integer in range

commonMistakes: Using Math.random() for cryptographic or security purposes — use crypto.getRandomValues() instead

entries.name: new Map()
entries.description: Creates a new Map object that holds key-value pairs. Keys can be any type. Maintains insertion order. More performant than objects for frequent additions/deletions.

parameters.name: iterable
parameters.description: An iterable of [key, value] pairs. Optional.

examples.title: Basic Map usage
Map from object entries

entries.name: Map.set()
entries.description: Adds or updates an entry in a Map with the specified key and value. Returns the Map itself (chainable).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to set. Can be any value.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to set.

examples.title: Set and chain

entries.name: Map.get()
entries.description: Returns the value associated with the specified key, or undefined if the key doesn't exist.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to look up.

examples.title: Look up a value

entries.name: new Set()
entries.description: Creates a Set — a collection of unique values. Any type can be stored. Adding a duplicate has no effect.

parameters.name: iterable
parameters.description: An iterable of values to initialize the Set with.

examples.title: Deduplicate an array
Set operations

entries.name: Date.now()
entries.description: Returns the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC (Unix Epoch).

examples.title: Measure execution time

entries.name: Date.toISOString()
entries.description: Returns a string in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ. Always UTC timezone.

examples.title: Format current time
examples.code:
const now = new Date();
console.log(now.toISOString()); // '2024-01-15T09:30:00.000Z'

entries.name: RegExp.test()
entries.description: Executes a search for a match between a regular expression and a specified string. Returns true or false.

parameters.name: str
parameters.description: The string against which to match the regular expression.

examples.title: Validate email format
Check numeric string
examples.code:
const isNumber = /^\d+$/.test('12345');
console.log(isNumber); // true

entries.name: new Error()
entries.description: Creates a new Error object. Errors capture a stack trace and are used with throw/try/catch for exception handling.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Human-readable description of the error.

parameters.name: options.cause
parameters.description: Error cause for error chaining.

examples.title: Throw and catch
Custom error types
